classes.name: Elezzjoni Ġenerali (Kamra tad-Deputati)
classes.finest_note: The commission counts all ballots of a division together; results and every STV count are published by electoral division only.
classes.note: 65 members from thirteen five-member electoral divisions by the single transferable vote (Constitution art. 56; General Elections Act art. 17), plus bonus seats for the party with a majority of first preferences when the count leaves it short (art. 52) and up to twelve seats for the under-represented sex since 2021 (art. 52A). The commission's archive starts with the 1921 Legislative Assembly and includes the 1939 and 1945 Council of Government elections.

cadence.vacancy_rule: A casual election re-counts the vacating member's ballots among the unelected candidates of the division (General Elections Act, Thirteenth Schedule)

classes.name: Referendum nazzjonali
classes.finest_note: The commission publishes national totals only.
classes.note: Referendums under the Referenda Act of 1973: on proposals in a House resolution, on bills under Constitution art. 66(3) (never held), and abrogative referendums on a law requested by electors (Part V, added 2002). Earlier colonial votes in 1870, 1956, and 1964 were called by the government of the day.

classes.name: Elezzjoni tal-Kunsilli Lokali
classes.finest_note: Each locality is one division counted together; published by locality only.
classes.note: Councillors elected by the single transferable vote (Local Government Act art. 8(1)); from 1993 councils were renewed in groups on a rolling calendar, and since 2019 all 68 councils vote together with the European Parliament election, every five years. The mayor is the councillor of the majority party with most first-count votes (art. 4).

cadence.locator: https://legislation.mt/eli/cap/363/eng/pdf (art. 8(1): every five years; art. 8(6): on the same day of the Elections for the European Parliament)
cadence.vacancy_rule: A casual election re-counts the ballots of the vacating councillor, or the council co-opts (art. 9 and Third Schedule)

classes.name: Elezzjoni tal-Kumitati Amministrattivi
classes.finest_note: Each community is one division; published by community only.
classes.note: Committees for the communities of the Ninth Schedule, elected with the local councils by the single transferable vote; since Act XIV of 2019 a councillor resident in the community is assigned to it instead (art. 47A(5)).

access.evidence: Community committee elections by community, with each candidate's votes at every count.

classes.name: Referendum lokali
classes.note: Electors of a locality may seek the abrogation of a council bye-law by referendum under Part V of the Referenda Act, applied by art. 36A of the Local Government Act. None is known to have been held.

classes.name: Elezzjoni tal-Kunsill tal-Gvern (1849-1903)
classes.note: Elected members of the colonial Council of Government under the constitutions of 1849, 1887, and 1903, chosen by restricted franchises in districts; abolished with the 1921 self-government constitution.

dates.note: Not enumerated: no official list of these elections has been reached. Date not quoted from an official source: the Electoral Commission's results index, which lists it, refused this census's requests.

classes.name: Senat (1921-1933)
classes.note: Upper house of the 1921 self-government constitution: of 17 senators, 7 were elected by voters with property or education qualifications and 10 by special bodies (clergy, nobility, graduates, chamber of commerce, trade unions); abolished when the constitution was revoked in 1933.
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of the Senate results has been found; the Electoral Commission's archive, which lists the Legislative Assembly elections of 1921-1932, refused this census, so whether it holds the Senate is unconfirmed.

classes.name: Kunsill Ċiviku ta' Għawdex
classes.note: An elected council for Gozo and Comino set up in 1961 and dissolved in 1973 after a Gozo referendum.
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of its results has been found among the sources this census could reach; the Electoral Commission's archive refused this census.

classes.name: Referendum tal-Kunsill Ċiviku ta' Għawdex (1973)
classes.note: Gozo's electors were asked whether to keep the Gozo Civic Council; it was dissolved after the vote.
classes.disposition_reason: No official publication of the result has been found among the sources this census could reach; the Electoral Commission's archive refused this census.

classes.name: Elezzjonijiet każwali
classes.note: A vacancy is filled by re-counting the vacating member's ballots among the candidates who stood unsuccessfully (General Elections Act, Thirteenth Schedule; Local Government Act art. 9).
classes.disposition_reason: No elector votes: the commission re-counts ballots already cast at the general or local election, so the count adds no votes beyond the original contest.

classes.name: Sindku
classes.note: The mayor is the councillor of the party with an absolute majority of councillors who had the most first-count votes; otherwise the councillors elect one by open ballot (Local Government Act art. 4 and Seventh Schedule).
classes.disposition_reason: No separate ballot: the mayor follows from the council count or is chosen by the councillors.

classes.name: Kunsilli Reġjonali
classes.note: Six regional councils (art. 37A) made up of a representative named by each mayor, chaired by a President of the Region elected from among the region's councillors; regional committees existed from 1993 and councils from 2011.
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect: members are appointed by the local councils and the president is chosen by councillors, not by the electorate.

classes.name: President ta' Malta
classes.note: Appointed by a resolution of the House supported by two thirds of its members (Constitution art. 48(1)) for a five-year term; before 2020 by a simple majority resolution.
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect: chosen by the House of Representatives, not by the electorate.

classes.name: Imħallfin u Maġistrati
classes.note: Appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister after the Judicial Appointments Committee's assessment (Constitution arts. 96 and 100).

classes.name: Għażla tal-kandidati
classes.note: Parties choose their candidates and leaders under their own statutes.
classes.disposition_reason: The state runs no primary; nomination under the General Elections Act is by nomination paper, and party ballots are internal.

classes.name: Assoċjazzjoni tal-Kunsilli Lokali
classes.note: The association every council belongs to (art. 37(3)); its president and executive are chosen by councillors.
classes.disposition_reason: Indirect: chosen by local councillors, not by the electorate.
